reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: The crust does not change the wetted surface or near-wall flow, so friction versus a clean foul-release coating is unchanged; the 76% is a peak-gel-stress reduction relative to the parent, not a drag gain.
key_assumption_issues: Baseline is the thin-crust parent, not a standard foul-release coating; against standard silicone the comparison would need strength, not stress.
Pasternak (shear-only) crust ignores crust bending and the Gaussian load idealisation of bristles; real bristles sweep and add tangential loads.
Only point loads benefit; blunt fender contacts, the most damaging events, are not reduced.
killer_risks: Crust/gel delamination under sweeping brush tangential loads and impacts (gel cohesion < 0.1 MPa).
A 5 MPa fibre-reinforced crust stiffens the surface for peel, reducing fouling release for small foulers and slime.
Thick multi-layer silicone system is expensive.

requirement_coverage.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirement_coverage.reason: Biocide-free foul release, somewhat weaker release than the uncrusted gel.

requirement_coverage.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirement_coverage.reason: Credible protection against grooming and grit; blunt impacts and delamination remain.

requirement_coverage.name: low_consumption_operation
requirement_coverage.reason: Passive; makes in-water cleaning possible without damage.

requirement_coverage.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirement_coverage.reason: Sprayable but thick, multi-layer and fibre-filled; costly.

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: No effect on friction; and the concept's own simulation shows the nm layer on a hard substrate shares load worse than a soft silicone film, so even the fouling-release claim is doubtful.
key_assumption_issues: Elastic interface stiffness 1e10 Pa/m is a free, optimistic parameter; an elastic nm hydration layer is orders of magnitude stiffer.
Hydration lubrication requires hydrated surfaces on both sides; barnacle and mussel cements displace bound water and bind to zwitterions.
The steady model cannot represent viscous sliding, the only mechanism by which the concept could work.
killer_risks: Fouling adhesives bind through or displace the brush; release becomes worse than on silicone.
Brush reservoir depletes with abrasion within a few years; hydrolysis of anchors.
Hard PU base gives no compliance for release.

requirement_coverage.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirement_coverage.reason: Non-toxic, good against microfouling, likely poor release of hard macrofouling.

requirement_coverage.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirement_coverage.reason: Self-replenishing reservoir helps but is finite; hydrolysis and abrasion.

requirement_coverage.name: low_consumption_operation
requirement_coverage.reason: Passive; the reservoir is consumed slowly and reapplication is likely at each docking.

reviews.plausible_gain_reasoning: A levelled silicone overcoat is at best as smooth as standard foul release, so friction is unchanged (and bead waviness could add ~0.5-1% if levelling is poor); the 50% is a fouling-release stress reduction.
key_assumption_issues: Metric is fouling detachment stress, not drag.
Guth-Gold stiffening and mean compliance average over bead crests, where compliance is ~2x lower and barnacles anchor.
Gouge protection by beads is asserted, not modelled.
killer_risks: Thin skin over bead crests abrades first, exposing hard beads that foul and roughen the surface.
Poor levelling on a 1e4 m2 hull leaves waviness > 10 um, turning the coating into a rough surface.
Bead/silicone debonding and water ingress along beads after damage.

requirement_coverage.name: low_friction_drag
requirement_coverage.reason: No reduction; smoothness at risk from bead waviness.

requirement_coverage.name: non_toxic_antifouling
requirement_coverage.reason: Biocide-free silicone surface with lower release stress than standard.

requirement_coverage.name: multi_year_seawater_durability
requirement_coverage.reason: Aggregate improves resistance to blunt loads; crest wear and debonding remain.

requirement_coverage.name: hull_scale_applicability
requirement_coverage.reason: Broadcast aggregate is an established dock technique; extra layers and QA of levelling add cost.
